ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Evel Knievel

code.originalText: Cure confirmed (SVR12): six-month liver cancer surveillance, cirrhosis care after cure, and transplant criteria reviewed

text.paragraph: Test of cure for hepatitis C and six-month liver cancer surveillance. [S]

Mr. Knievel returns 13 weeks after his last dose of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir. The surveillance ultrasound a week ago showed no liver lesion. He had the zoledronic acid infusion eleven weeks ago, with a day of aches afterwards. His eye examination in June showed no diabetic retinopathy. He has had no alcohol since February. He takes carvedilol 12.5 mg daily. Pain is about 4 of 10 and he walks 30 minutes most days. He has had no falls, abdominal swelling, black stools, confusion or yellow eyes. He has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-08-17; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 82.6 kg; blood pressure 120/74, pulse 60
A few spider angiomas; no jaundice

Raised transaminases (ALT 88, AST 96 U/L) and low platelets (118) on today's tests, with spider angiomas and palmar erythema, in a man of 57 who received many blood transfusions after crashes before 1992 and drinks most evenings: chronic liver disease, most likely hepatitis C, must be excluded. Hepatitis C antibody with reflex RNA, hepatitis A and B serology, HIV, liver ultrasound and hepatology review ordered
S — Synthetic presenting problem; no symptom or result of his real illness was made public. Superseded at the hepatology consultation.

Chronic hepatitis C, genotype 1a, treatment-naive, HCV RNA 2.35 million IU/mL, likely acquired through blood transfusions after crashes; synthetic modern detail linked to his publicly reported transfusion-acquired hepatitis C
S — Synthetic genotype, viral load and timing; his hepatitis C and its likely transfusion source are documented (D).

Compensated cirrhosis from hepatitis C, with alcohol as a cofactor: liver stiffness 26.8 kPa, FIB-4 4.94, nodular liver and a 14.2 cm spleen on ultrasound, platelets 118; Child-Pugh A5, MELD-Na 8; no ascites, encephalopathy, jaundice or bleeding
S — Synthetic stage of liver disease linked to his documented hepatitis C and later liver transplant.
Clinically significant portal hypertension in compensated cirrhosis (liver stiffness 25 kPa or more), treated with carvedilol without screening endoscopy (Baveno VII)
S — Synthetic finding at the hepatology consultation.
S — Synthetic; diabetes is documented only in his last years (D), and placing it at 57 is a synthetic choice.
Chronic pain in the back, hips, pelvis and knees after dozens of fractures from stunt crashes, including a broken pelvis; ibuprofen stopped, and managed without oral NSAIDs or opioids
S — Synthetic pain at the index age, anchored to his documented fractures and the pain of his later years.
Osteoporosis in a man with cirrhosis, prior heavy alcohol use and dozens of old fractures: femoral neck T-score -2.6, lumbar spine -1.9
S — Synthetic finding before the bone density scan.

list.item:
Chronic hepatitis C, cured (sustained virologic response) (B18.2). HCV RNA not detected 13 weeks after a 12-week course, with ALT 22 and AST 26 U/L: virologic and biochemical cure. The antibody will stay positive for life, so any future check for reinfection must be an HCV RNA test. [S]
Problem resolved.
HCV RNA if liver tests rise or a new exposure occurs.

Compensated cirrhosis after cure (K74.69). Child-Pugh A5 (bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL, albumin 4.0 g/dL, INR 1.0) and MELD-Na 6; platelets 134, rising; FIB-4 now 2.36. Cure lowers but does not remove the risk of liver cancer and decompensation in cirrhosis. No transplant evaluation: there has been no decompensation and the MELD-Na is far below 15. [S]
Ultrasound with alpha-fetoprotein every six months for life; next in February.
Liver stiffness and platelets a year after cure, to see whether portal hypertension has improved.
No alcohol.

Clinically significant portal hypertension (K76.6). Continue carvedilol until reassessment a year after cure. [S]
Carvedilol 12.5 mg daily.

Type 2 diabetes (E11.65). Glucose management indicator 6.8%, A1c 6.3%, fasting glucose 112 mg/dL; no hypoglycemia; no retinopathy. [S]
Continue metformin and the sensor.

Osteoporosis (M81.8). Zoledronic acid given; no falls. [S]
